slides.title: Does your skin suit feel wrong on race day?
slides.sub: Size it for your skating position, not the mirror

slides.title: A skin suit is not clothing
slides.body: Normal clothes are cut larger than you. A skin suit has negative ease: it is cut smaller and stretches on, so the fabric works under tension.

slides.title: Standing upright misleads you
slides.caption: Comfortable standing usually means too big, while snug in position means correct.

slides.title: Run three checks in position
slides.body: Can you breathe fully into your ribs? Does the crotch seam stay put on a full sideways extension? Does the shoulder pull when you swing an arm across?

slides.title: Do not buy a size up
slides.body: An oversized suit stops compressing and the leg grippers cannot grip. Between sizes, go smaller, unless the smaller size restricts your breathing.

slides.title: Wash cold, dry in shade
slides.body: Rinse in cold water soon after a session. Wash inside out, skip fabric softener, never tumble dry, and dry flat or on a hanger in shade.

slides.text: Buy for the position, not the mirror.
